steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: WARNING — Electrical Shock Hazard. Disconnect power before servicing.

steps.title: Dispenser mechanical check
steps.body: Clear obstructions preventing dispenser lid from opening. If all TRIAC loads dead, check door switch, F500, pilot relay.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Clear obstructions preventing dispenser lid from opening. If all TRIAC loads dead, check door switch, F500, pilot relay.

steps.title: Disconnect P12
steps.body: Power off. Remove outer door and toe panels. Unplug P12 from control.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Power off. Remove outer door and toe panels. Unplug P12 from control.

steps.title: Dispenser solenoid 310–380 Ω?
steps.body: Ohms between P12-5 and P12-7. Expected 310–380 Ω per strip circuit.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Ohms between P12-5 and P12-7. Expected 310–380 Ω per strip circuit.

steps.title: Reconnect P12 and restore power
steps.body: Reconnect P12. Restore power for Service Diagnostics live test.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Reconnect P12. Restore power for Service Diagnostics live test.

steps.title: Continue after Service Diagnostics entry
steps.body: Service Diagnostics cycle should be available (entered via key sequence; cycle starts when door closes). Continue with bench checks below.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Refer to Component Testing; use Service Diagnostics Cycle for live load verification.

steps.title: Dispenser energizes in Service Diagnostics?
steps.body: 120 VAC at P12-5 to P12-7 during dispenser interval (solenoid connected).
steps.sourceExcerpt: 120 VAC at P12-5 to P12-7 during dispenser interval (solenoid connected).

steps.title: Replace dispenser solenoid
steps.body: Replace dispenser solenoid or repair harness.
steps.oemOutcome: Replace dispenser solenoid or repair harness.

steps.title: Replace ACU
steps.body: Solenoid good but no AC drive — replace control.
steps.oemOutcome: Solenoid good but no AC drive — replace control.
